Places: how crowded an address is, and what kind of place it is

Source: R/md-places.R
md_build_places.Rd

Builds the place tables dev/PLACES.md describes, so the matching side knows for any address how many organisations report it, in how many suites, and whether it is a national office, a fiscal sponsor's mail drop, a multi-tenant building or an organisation with its foundation. npmatch labels addresses the same way at run time (np_addr_freq(), branch fix/address-class); these tables add what it cannot see.

Usage

md_build_places(
  con,
  share_min = 10L,
  unit_coverage_min = 0.5,
  top_share_min = 0.5,
  flag_share = 0.5,
  building_digits = 4L
)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection with address, address_derived and entity; name/name_derived (or name_compact), entity_group and the geocode columns are used when present.

share_min, unit_coverage_min, top_share_min

npmatch's class thresholds (its defaults): crowded at share_min occupants; a building needs two suites and unit_coverage_min of occupants naming one; federated at top_share_min of occupants under one name.

flag_share

Share at which a flag's evidence counts (PMB suites, care-of agents, one group ruling, churn). To be measured on the full database (dev/PLACES.md section 9).

building_digits

Decimal places rooftop coordinates are rounded to for a building id. 4 is about 11 m of latitude; to be measured.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

Details

It writes three tables:

place

One row per address that two or more EINs report as their own current address. A lookup miss means one occupant, which is about 88% of addresses.

place_layer

(place_key, layer, n_eins). Layers partition EINs, so the count for any selection of layers - active only, unified - is an exact sum, as with ein_key_layer.

place_unit

One row per suite that two or more EINs at a place share.

Who counts as an occupant

An EIN occupies a place when the place is its own current address: an address row of class mailing or principal (the BMF, the latest 990 header, the e-Postcard). A grantmaker writing a grantee's address (class observed) is not occupancy, and an old address (historical) counts only toward the history columns.

Keys

place_key is npmatch's address key - street_key, a space, zip5, empty for a PO box - and unit_id its suite identifier ("STE D-2" -> D2), so a lookup from npmatch never misses on spelling. See md_place_key().

Columns of place

n_eins

occupants

n_name_keys, top_name_share

distinct legal name keys among the occupants, and the share holding the commonest one: one name dominating is a national office, names spread is a sponsor or agent

n_units, max_eins_per_unit, n_eins_with_unit, unit_coverage

recorded suites. Coverage travels with the count: at 1,601 crowded BMF addresses no record names a suite, and "several suites" can describe the data as easily as the building

n_pmb_units, pmb_share

private-mailbox suites, and the share of occupants with a suite whose suite is a PMB

n_group_exemptions, share_in_largest_group, has_group_central

the IRS group rulings among the occupants: a national office its chapters file from, confirmed without reading names

n_care_of_agents, care_of_agent_share, bank_trust_share

occupants whose in-care-of name is an agent (bank, trust company, CPA, law firm), by the word list care_of_network uses

n_eins_ever, first_year, last_year, churn

every EIN that has had the place as its own address, current or historical, and the share no longer there

building_id, n_place_keys_in_building

rooftop geocodes rounded to building_digits decimals: one building written two ways

place_class

npmatch's four labels by npmatch's rule and thresholds: federated, building, shared, cluster

flag_*, place_flags

what only matchdb sees: cmra, care_of, bank_trust, group_confirmed, agent_churn, military_or_gd

class_rule, normalize_signature

the stamps
